Women who are treated for hypothyroidism during their menstrual cycle or within 6 months of completing treatment are not at any increased risk for perinatal morbidity. However, they may be more susceptible to complications such as gestational diabetes and preeclampsia due to potential thyroid hormone imbalances throughout the year.

It is essential to note that untreated hypothyroidism can increase the risk of pregnancy complications, particularly if left unmanaged. Women with hypothyroidism should be closely monitored during pregnancy and under close medical supervision to minimize risks and ensure proper care for both mother and baby.
